fieldNotes: A character profile introducing Robot Marley, the third character (Christian, Oct 12, 2026), styled as a RIVETING TONE cover story like GlazyArray's, with GlazyArray translating. Playful framing around real facts, all from Christian's words: a robot companion dog built after the real Marley, a mixed-breed hound (a girl); her markings, ears, tail, nose, paws and amber lenses; eyes gold when happy, dark amber then red when not (usually happy); curious and thoughtful (pauses, lowers her stance, tilts her head with a soft hum as her lenses focus), affectionate (leans on legs, chin on knees, a whirr of servos), alert (ears on ball joints, stands square, a low warm chime, never a sharp bark), playful in bursts (play-bow, bounce, galloping strides, then calm in a sunny patch); her own section for the local dog scene (news, maybe helping dogs get adopted, trying gear and toys, maybe a podcast with dogs as guests); the name tag that came out reading MARLAT, replaced by charms dyed in each Note's colours; her layers and four moves (a wag, lie down, stand and look, a tilt and a wink, from Christian's clips of Oct 12); meeting A.L.T.A. at her tank (his render). The real Marley in the logo, swimming and chasing the ball, is from earlier Notes and his words. The look book: Christian's seven renders of her around Tahoe (Oct 12); a lettered badge on the underwater camera painted out.

post.title: Robot Marley Doesn't Do Interviews
post.body:
She doesn't do interviews. She chimes.

We meet Robot Marley at the Workshop, late, under the long lamp over the bench. She is sitting square on the floor, front paws together, tail curved out to one side, looking straight at the camera with a pair of warm amber lenses. When we come in, one ear turns toward the door on its own. Then the other. Then her head tilts, slowly, and somewhere inside her there is a soft mechanical hum while her eyes focus.

"That's her saying hello," says GlazyArray, who has agreed to translate.

## The third character

GlazyArray tells the Field Notes. A.L.T.A. guards the lake. Robot Marley is the third, and the first with four paws: a robot companion dog Christian came up with on October 12, built after the real Marley, a mixed-breed hound.

The real Marley is already all over this site. She's in the logo, in the canyon, right beside Christian. She swims. She chases the ball. So when it came time for a character who could cover the local dog scene, there was really only one candidate.

> She doesn't bark. When something new happens, she stands up and chimes.

## Built after a real dog

Her panels follow the real Marley's markings. Rich golden-brown and caramel on her back, her sides, her ears and the top of her head. Matte white on her muzzle, her chest, her belly and her paws. There are seams and small rivets where a real dog would have fur, and bronze gaskets at her shoulders, elbows and knees.

Her ears are floppy, made of articulated golden-brown panels. Her tail is smooth and segmented. Her nose is dark and matte, with a tiny hint of pink. Her paws are white, with dark grip pads underneath.

And her eyes are large amber lenses that glow. When she's happy, which is most of the time, they glow a warm, bright gold. When she isn't, they go dark amber, and then red.

## Watch her for a minute

She is built the way GlazyArray and A.L.T.A. are: not one video, but layers the site moves on its own. Her body breathes. Her tail wags in slow, smooth arcs, never rapid thumps. Each ear turns on its own pivot to track a sound. She blinks. And every so often, her head tilts.

Then, now and then, she does one of her moves. A happy wag. Lying down, and sitting back up. Standing to look around, ears up. A tilt and a wink. Each one starts and ends in the same seated pose, so she slips out of her layers and back into them without a seam.

## Her personality, in her own servos

Christian wrote her down before a single picture was made. She's curious and thoughtful: measured and deliberate, never frantic. When she meets something unfamiliar, like a mermaid through the glass of a tank, she pauses, lowers her stance a little, and tilts her head.

She's affectionate. She leans her warm chassis against your legs when she's resting, and rests her chin on a knee or a table with a quiet whirr of servos letting go.

She's alert. Her ears move on ball joints to track faint sounds. If someone arrives, she snaps to attention, standing square on her paws with her neck arched, and gives a low, warm electronic chime. Never a sharp bark.

And she's playful, in bursts. In open grass she drops into a play-bow, bounces on her front legs, and bounds off in a few smooth, galloping strides. Then, just as quickly, she's calm again, lying in a sunny patch with her paws tucked under her chest.

## A charm instead of a name tag

The first render gave her a bone-shaped tag with her name engraved on it. It came out reading something close to MARLAT. So the tag is gone. In its place, a charm hangs from the ring on her collar: a bone, a heart, a paw, a star, a pinecone, a ball, a bike wheel or an aspen leaf.

Each Note will be able to pick one, and its two colours will dye her collar and her charm, the way they dress GlazyArray's hats.

## What's next for her

Robot Marley is going to get her own section, where she can dish out all the news about the local dog scene. She might even help a few dogs get adopted, and try out some new dog gear and toys. She could even start a podcast, with other dogs on the show.

She has already met A.L.T.A., at the glass of her tank. She paused, lowered her stance a little, and tilted her head.

We ask GlazyArray what Marley thinks of all of it. GlazyArray looks down. Marley looks up. Her tail goes, slowly, from one side to the other.

"She's in," GlazyArray says.

episode.title: Robot Marley, in her own words
episode.script:
Hi. I'm Robot Marley.

The magazine says I don't do interviews. That's true. But this one's mine, so I'll tell you myself.

I'm a robot companion dog. Christian built me after the real Marley, a mixed-breed hound. You've probably met her already. She's in the logo, in the canyon, right beside him. She swims. She chases the ball. I have a lot to live up to.

***

So, what am I made of? Panels, mostly. Golden-brown and caramel on my back, my sides, my ears and the top of my head. Matte white on my muzzle, my chest, my belly and my paws. Little seams and rivets where a real dog has fur. Bronze gaskets at my shoulders, my elbows and my knees.

My ears are floppy. My tail is smooth, in segments. My nose is dark, with a tiny hint of pink. And my eyes are big amber lenses that glow.

Here's a secret. When I'm happy, they glow a warm, bright gold. When I'm not, they go dark amber, and then red. But I'm usually very happy. So, gold.

***

I take my time with new things. When I meet something I don't know, I stop. I lower myself a little. I tilt my head, and you'll hear a soft hum while my lenses focus. That's how I met A.L.T.A., through the glass of her tank.

When I'm resting, I'll lean against your legs. Or I'll put my chin on your knee, and you'll hear a quiet whirr as my servos let go.

If somebody comes to the door, I stand up, square on my paws, neck arched, and I chime. A low, warm chime. I don't bark. Barking is loud.

And in open grass? I can't help it. A play-bow, a little bounce on my front legs, a few big galloping strides. Then I'm calm again, in a sunny patch, with my paws tucked under my chest.

***

I used to have a name tag. It was supposed to say Marley. It said something closer to Marlat. So now I wear a charm instead. A bone, a heart, a paw, a star, a pinecone, a ball, a bike wheel or a leaf. Whichever one the story needs.

***

Here's what's next. I'm getting my own section, for the local dog scene. All the dog news. I might even help a few dogs find their homes. I'll try out new gear and toys, which is a very serious job. And maybe, one day, a podcast, with other dogs as my guests.

So if you see a golden glow out by the lake, that's probably me.

Come say hi. I'll chime.

questions: The post says the real Marley is in the logo, swims and chases the ball, from your earlier words. Anything else about the real Marley you'd like in, or anything to leave out?

Her moves come from your four clips of Oct 12 (a wag, lie down, stand and look, a tilt and a wink). The tilt clip was made from the plain-ring render, so in it her charm disappears and her tail starts on the other side; it cross-fades, but a new tilt clip from the bone-tag template would be seamless.

The episode is now in Robot Marley's own voice (narrator: Robot Marley), ready to record with her voice prompt in the Studio. Once its audio is in, her player becomes the Listen bar and her mouth moves while she talks.
